learnings.question: According to a hadith recorded in the 40 Hadith of an-Nawawi collection, leaving aside one specific thing is described as part of the perfection of a person's Islam. What is that thing?
options: That which does not concern him
learnings.learning: The Prophet Muhammad said that part of the perfection of a person's Islam is leaving what does not concern him, as recorded in the 40 Hadith of an-Nawawi — a reminder to filter out distractions that don't serve your real priorities.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: A personal website's automated content-curation script decides whether to keep or discard a daily YouTube video by asking one specific question about the viewer. Which group does that question specifically describe?
options: A tech entrepreneur based in Silicon Valley
A university student studying computer science
A Muslim, Malaysian software engineer early in his career
A general audience interested in self-help
learnings.learning: A personal website runs a script that filters YouTube videos daily by asking whether a Muslim, Malaysian software engineer early in his career would actually benefit from watching it — if not, it's discarded automatically.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: What term, coined from research behind the 'Google Effect' paper, describes the way our brains stop retaining information once it has been written down or stored digitally?
learnings.learning: Researchers behind the 'Google Effect' study describe 'Digital Amnesia' — the tendency for our brains to stop retaining information once it's been written down or stored digitally, since we trust the external record to remember it for us.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: A 19th-century researcher demonstrated that people forget roughly 80% of newly learned material within 24 hours unless they actively recall it, a finding that underpins spaced-repetition learning. Who was this researcher?
learnings.learning: In the 1880s, Hermann Ebbinghaus found that people forget about 80% of newly learned material within 24 hours unless they actively work to recall it — the basis for spaced-repetition learning.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: Which three roles make up a classic Scrum team?
options: Product Owner, Business Analyst, and QA Lead
Product Owner, Scrum Master, and Developers
Project Manager, Team Lead, and Developers
learnings.learning: A Scrum team is built around three key roles: the Product Owner, who prioritizes the backlog; the Scrum Master, who protects the team from distractions; and the Developers, who build the product.

learnings.question: In the Scrum framework, what is the main purpose of breaking a project into short, iterative cycles called Sprints?
options: To eliminate the need for planning meetings
To reduce the number of team members needed
To allow for more flexibility and quicker adjustments
To increase the overall length of the project
learnings.learning: Scrum breaks a project into short, iterative cycles called Sprints specifically to allow for more flexibility and quicker adjustments than a single long development cycle would.

learnings.question: A specific verse states that Allah created jinn and mankind for one singular purpose. What is that stated purpose?
learnings.learning: The Quran (51:56) states that Allah created jinn and mankind for a singular purpose: to worship Him, which in Islamic theology extends beyond ritual to recognizing His sovereignty and living with gratitude.

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, what Arabic term refers to humanity's role as stewards or caretakers of the Earth?
learnings.learning: In Islam, humans are described as khalifah — stewards or caretakers of the Earth — a role that carries responsibility for preserving faith and unity, not just personal conduct.

learnings.question: In Islamic teaching on accountability, what is the smallest unit of good or evil deed said to still be recorded and ultimately seen by its doer?
learnings.learning: The Quran (99:7-8) teaches that no deed, however small, goes unaccounted for — stating that whoever does even an atom's weight of good or evil will see its consequence.

learnings.question: In PCIe power management, which state represents a device that is almost completely powered down, used for the longest periods of inactivity, with the highest power savings but the longest wake-up time?
learnings.learning: In PCIe power management, L2 is the deepest power-saving state — the device is almost completely powered down, giving the highest energy savings but the longest time to wake back up.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: In an analogy comparing PCIe power states to everyday computer power modes, which low-power PCIe state is compared to a computer's screen turning off, remaining able to quickly resume full operation?
learnings.learning: PCIe's L0s state is compared to a computer screen turning off: the device becomes less active but can resume full operation almost immediately, unlike deeper sleep states.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, which term refers to Allah's complete, eternal, pre-written plan and knowledge of all events, as distinct from how those events actually unfold in a person's life?
learnings.learning: In Islamic theology, Qadr refers to Allah's complete and eternal foreknowledge of every event, while Qada' is how those events actually unfold in a person's life, in part shaped by supplication and effort.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: A well-known Quranic verse states that Allah does not change the condition of a people until what happens?
options: Until a prophet is sent to them
Until they change what is in themselves
Until they make the pilgrimage to Mecca
learnings.learning: Surah Ar-Ra'd (13:11) states that Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is within themselves, framing personal transformation as a precursor to a changed outcome.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: A Python-based word-frequency analysis tested whether the Pareto Principle (the 80/20 rule) applies to the Quran's text. What percentage of the Quran did the top 20 most frequent words actually account for?
learnings.learning: A Python-based word-frequency analysis of the Quran found that the top 20 most frequent words account for only about 20.83% of the total text, far short of the 80% a Pareto (80/20) assumption might predict.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: What is the term for the small diacritical markings placed above or below Arabic letters to indicate vowel sounds and pronunciation?
learnings.learning: Tashkeel are the small diacritical marks placed above or below Arabic letters to indicate vowel sounds — without them, the same string of consonants can be read multiple ways.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python
